archetypes.name: script-corpus
archetypes.rationale: The A1 scanner's safety guarantee depends entirely on an explicit enumerated file set; a wrong basename, missing path, or incorrect exclusion silently drops timing coverage without CI signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether every script in the A1 scanner enumeration (implement-bootstrap.sh, step2-implement.sh, commit-implementation.sh, commit-review-fixes.sh, step-7a.sh, refresh-run-logs.sh, implement-finalize.sh, step-telemetry-mark.sh, run-step5-review.sh, run-relevant-checks-captured.sh, launch-codex-implement.sh, launch-cursor-implement.sh, launch-codex-ci.sh, launch-cursor-ci.sh, launch-claude-ci.sh) actually exists at the stated paths and actually emits timing-ledger.sh or timing-report.sh calls. Verify the excluded pair (launch-review.sh, launch-claude-subprocess.sh) either contain no implement-scoped timing calls or contain calls that must not be mis-pinned to =implement. Confirm the five A2 pin targets each have a record-vendor-task line syntactically compatible with the DESIGN_TMPDIR='' LARCH_TIMING_SKILL=implement prefix shape the plan prescribes. Flag any name mismatches, missing paths, or evidence that the enumerated set is incomplete or over-inclusive. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: python-stub-fit
archetypes.rationale: Item B's proposed tests depend on a specific RecordingRunner stub shape and Outcome.TRANSIENT routing path that must match the actual current test_ci_monitor.py source; incorrect assumptions make the stubs non-compilable or silently wrong.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify item B's test design against the actual python/test_ci_monitor.py source: check the RecordingRunner stub (referenced at lines 330-351) to confirm it accepts the gh-pr-view rc=1 shape the plan describes and that consecutive status-gather errors route to Outcome.TRANSIENT rather than Outcome.STALLED. Check whether monitor() has an already_merged short-circuit that yields Outcome.OK, and whether the plan's assert-detail claim of '3 times consecutively' is consistent with how monitor() actually formats its detail field. If any plan-assumed behavior does not match the current source, flag it as a plan defect since the test will either fail to compile or assert the wrong outcome. Also check whether the ~30-60 LOC budget is plausible given the test patterns the plan prescribes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
